text: Type hints become truly powerful when a tool like mypy checks them for you.
mypy reads your type annotations and finds mismatches without ever running your code.
greet promises to take a string and return a string, and total expects a list of integers.
[chuckle] If you called greet with the number forty-two, mypy would flag it as an error before you ran anything.
[sniff] It catches a whole class of bugs — passing the wrong type — at your desk, not in production.
Correct usage type-checks silently, giving you confidence the pieces fit together.
[sigh] Optional makes the possibility of None explicit, forcing you to handle the empty case.
So find, which might return a string or None, documents that honestly for both readers and the checker.
[groan] On large codebases, static type checking catches countless mistakes early — it's like a spellchecker for your logic.
